mainTopic: Animals from traps on יום טוב, and when a גוי's gift brought on יום טוב is permitted
overview: A ברייתא teaches that on יום טוב one may slaughter animals from pens, but not animals found in nets or traps, since they may have been caught on יום טוב itself. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains that traps found sprung before יום טוב are permitted, but a case of doubt is treated as caught on יום טוב and is forbidden. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules like him. The גמרא then asks what רבן גמליאל meant in the משנה when he said a גוי's gift of fish is 'permitted.' רב says it may only be received, and לוי says it may even be eaten. רב explains that both heard רבי rule 'eat' in the evening, but only רב was there in the morning when רבי changed it to 'receive.' A ברייתא about a גוי's gift of fresh fish and fruit is shown to be about food that only looks fresh, so it fits both views. רב פפא gives the practical rule: if that kind of produce is still attached to the ground, the gift is forbidden, even after יום טוב for the time picking would take. If none is still growing and it came from within the תחום, it is permitted, and his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pens are fine, traps are not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that on יום טוב one may slaughter animals from pens, but not animals found in nets or traps.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום טוב you may slaughter animals taken from pens, but not animals found in nets or traps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets out the basic rule: animals already kept in pens may be slaughtered on יום טוב, but animals found in nets and traps may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals in a pen were clearly caught and ready before יום טוב. Animals in a trap may have been caught on יום טוב itself, and trapping is forbidden on יום טוב, so they are not permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosed pens where animals are kept (with water pools)

phrases.english: One may slaughter from the pens on יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מִן הָרְשָׁתוֹת וּמִן הַמִּכְמוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: but not from the nets and from the traps.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals from pens may be slaughtered on יום טוב; animals from nets and traps may not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: when the trap was found sprung decides
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that if the traps were found sprung before יום טוב the animals are permitted, and if found sprung on יום טוב they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: if he came before יום טוב and found the traps sprung, we know the animals were caught before יום טוב, so they are permitted. If he came on יום טוב and found them sprung, we know they were caught on יום טוב, so they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds a more detailed rule: it all depends on when the person saw that the traps had caught something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sprung trap is a sign that an animal was caught. If that sign was already seen before יום טוב, the catching happened on a weekday and the animal is permitted. If the sign first showed up on יום טוב, the catching happened on יום טוב and the animal is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Disturbed or sprung, showing an animal was caught

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If he came and found them sprung on the eve of יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁמֵּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: it is known that they were caught on the eve of יום טוב, and they are permitted.
If he came and found them sprung on יום טוב,
it is known that they were caught on יום טוב, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detailed rule about trapped animals to the basic rule of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Traps found sprung before יום טוב: permitted. Traps found sprung on יום טוב: forbidden.

steps.title: From the first half: a doubtful case is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the first half of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule and infers that a doubtful case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement contradicts itself. You said: if he found them sprung before יום טוב, we know they were caught before יום טוב. The reason they are permitted is that he actually found them sprung then. So if we are not sure, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that the ברייתא has an inner contradiction, and starts by drawing an inference from its first half. This is the setup; the clash comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half only permits the animals when we saw the trap sprung before יום טוב. That suggests that without such proof, when we are unsure, the animals are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult (contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: You said: if he came and found them sprung on the eve of יום טוב,
it is known that they were caught on the eve of יום טוב.
The reason is that he came and found them sprung,
but if it is doubtful, they are forbidden.
phrases.notes: Doubtful here means we don't know if the animal got caught before יום טוב or on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the first half of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first half of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since permission depends on actually seeing the trap sprung before יום טוב, a doubtful case must be forbidden.

steps.title: From the second half: a doubtful case is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the second half and infers the opposite: a doubtful case is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now say the second half: if he found them sprung on יום טוב, we know they were caught on יום טוב. The reason they are forbidden is that he actually found them sprung on יום טוב. So if we are not sure, we assume they were caught before יום טוב, and they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge: the second half of the same statement seems to say that a doubtful case is permitted, which clashes with the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half only forbids the animals when we saw the trap sprung on יום טוב. That suggests that in a doubtful case they are permitted. So one statement seems to give two opposite rulings for the same doubtful case.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (of the same statement)

phrases.english: Say the last part:
If he came and found them sprung on יום טוב,
it is known that they were caught on יום טוב.
The reason is that he came and found them sprung,

phrases.aramaic: הָא סְפֵיקָא — מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: but if it is doubtful, they were caught on the eve of יום טוב, and they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction begun in step 3 by drawing the opposite inference from the second half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half implies a doubtful case is forbidden; the second half implies it is permitted. Both cannot be right.

steps.title: The second half is really about the doubtful case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the second half means: in a doubtful case, the animals are treated as caught on יום טוב and are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if he found them sprung before יום טוב, we know they were caught before יום טוב, and they are permitted. But if it is doubtful, it is treated as if they were caught on יום טוב, and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the statement: the second half is not about a certain case at all, but tells us how to treat the doubtful case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first half is a case of certainty. The second half's case, finding the traps sprung on יום טוב, is really a doubt, since we didn't see when the animal got caught. That doubt is treated like catching on יום טוב, so it is forbidden. Now both halves agree: doubt is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the answer as saying a found-on-יום-טוב trap is certainly caught on יום טוב. The point is that it is a doubt, and the doubt is treated like it was caught on יום טוב.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא וּמְצָאָן מְקוּלְקָלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If he came and found them sprung on the eve of יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁמֵּעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב נִצּוֹדוּ, וּמוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: it is known that they were caught on the eve of יום טוב, and they are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: הָא סְפֵיקָא — נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁנִּצּוֹדוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וַאֲסוּרִין.
phrases.english: But if it is doubtful, it is treated as if they were caught on יום טוב, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the second half as describing the doubtful case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both halves describe certain cases, so each implies a different ruling for doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the first half is certain; the second half is the doubt, which is treated as caught on יום טוב and forbidden.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling: we follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as just explained means: trapped animals are permitted only if the traps were seen sprung before יום טוב. If there is any doubt, the animals are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal found in a trap may be slaughtered on יום טוב only if it is known to have been caught before יום טוב. If it is unclear, it is treated as caught on יום טוב and is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the statement just clarified.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: trapped animals are permitted only when known to be caught before יום טוב; a doubtful case is forbidden.

steps.title: Permitted for what?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's words from the משנה, 'they are permitted,' and asks what exactly is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said: they are permitted. Permitted for what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks what רבן גמליאל meant by 'permitted.' This sets up the next step, where two answers are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Permitted' could mean only that you may accept the gift and move it. It could also mean that you may actually eat it. The word in the משנה does not tell us which one.

phrases.english: And he said: They are permitted.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן גמליאל in the משנה, talking about fish a גוי brought him on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Permitted for what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the traps case to another ruling in the משנה, about the gift from a גוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'permitted' means allowed to receive and move, or allowed to eat.

steps.title: רב says receive, לוי says eat
steps.stepSummary: רב says the fish may only be received. לוי says they may even be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: permitted to receive. לוי said: permitted to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, you may accept the gift and move it, but you may not eat it on יום טוב. According to לוי, you may also eat it. This is a real practical difference.

phrases.english: Rav said: They are permitted to be received.
And Levi said: They are permitted to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 7 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: only receiving is permitted. לוי: eating is also permitted.

steps.title: Never miss the study hall: how רב heard רבי change his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person should never stay away from the בית המדרש even for a moment. He proves it with this very argument: רבי changed his ruling in the morning, and only רב was there to hear it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person should never keep himself away from the study hall, even for one moment. Levi and I were with רבי when he taught this. In the evening he said 'permitted to eat.' In the morning he said 'permitted to receive.' I was in the study hall, so I changed my view. Levi was not there, so he did not change his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains how the argument with לוי started. Both of them first heard 'eat' from רבי, but only רב heard רבי change it to 'receive' the next morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows where each opinion comes from. לוי's view is רבי's first ruling, and רב's view is רבי's later ruling. That is why רב warns never to miss even one moment of learning.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's opinion ('receive only') is רבי's final ruling. לוי's opinion ('eat') is the ruling רבי taught first.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם
phrases.english: Rav said: A person should never hold back

phrases.aramaic: עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: himself from the study hall, even for one moment.
For Levi and I were in front of Rabbi
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who was the teacher of both of them.

phrases.english: when he said this teaching.
In the evening he said: They are permitted to be eaten;
in the morning he said: They are permitted to be received.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא — הֲדַרִי בִּי.
phrases.english: I, who was in the study hall, retracted.

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי דְּלָא הֲוָה בִּי מִדְרְשָׁא — לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Levi, who was not in the study hall, did not retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִמְנַע אָדָם עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the argument between רב and לוי in step 8 came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should never miss the study hall, even for one moment. Missing a moment can mean missing a change in a ruling.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא about a גוי's gift
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a גוי's gift, even fruit from that same day, is permitted. That fits רב, but fruit picked that day cannot be eaten, so how could לוי say 'eat'?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A גוי brought a gift to a Jew. Even moist fish and fruit from that day are permitted. This fits the one who says 'permitted to receive.' But according to the one who says 'permitted to eat,' is fruit from that day allowed to be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to support רב and contradict לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit picked on יום טוב itself is forbidden to eat. So the word 'permitted' in the ברייתא seems to mean only 'permitted to receive,' which is רב's view. That makes it hard to explain the ברייתא according to לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised a challenge (from an earlier source)

phrases.english: They challenged: A gentile who brought a gift to a Jew,
phrases.notes: He brought it on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ דָּגִים הַמְפוּלָּמִין וּפֵירוֹת בְּנֵי יוֹמָן — מוּתָּרִין.
phrases.english: even moist fish and fruit from that day are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוּתָּרִין לְקַבֵּל — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said 'permitted to be received,' it is fine.
But according to the one who said 'permitted to be eaten,'

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירוֹת בְּנֵי יוֹמָן מִי שָׁרוּ בַּאֲכִילָה?
phrases.english: is fruit from that day permitted to be eaten?
phrases.notes: Fruit picked on יום טוב itself is מוקצה, so it seems obvious that you could not eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to test the two opinions from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that the gift may be eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits fruit picked that same day. Such fruit cannot be eaten, so 'permitted' there must mean only receiving.

steps.title: Counter-question: can that fruit even be moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question back: by your own reasoning, fruit picked that day cannot even be moved. So the ברייתא is hard for רב's view too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning: is fruit from that day permitted to be moved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge. It shows that the challenge also creates a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit picked on יום טוב is מוקצה, so it may not even be moved. That means 'permitted to receive' would not work for that fruit either. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about fruit that was really picked that day.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ: פֵּירוֹת בְּנֵי יוֹמָן מִי שָׁרוּ בְּטִלְטוּל?
phrases.english: And according to your reasoning: is fruit from that day permitted to be moved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by showing that it also hits רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ברייתא clearly supports רב over לוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Fruit really picked that day cannot even be moved, so the ברייתא is a problem for both views.

steps.title: The ברייתא means fish and fruit that only look freshly caught or picked
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about fish whose gills are still red and fruit kept fresh in greens. It calls them 'from that day' because they look that fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing with fish whose gills are still red, and fruit preserved in greens. Why does it call them 'from that day'? Because they are like things from that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא in a new way. Now it causes no problem for לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish and fruit were not actually caught or picked on יום טוב. They only look fresh. So they are not מוקצה, and they may even be eaten. The ברייתא therefore fits לוי as well.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בני יומן' here does not mean the fruit was really picked that day. It only looks that fresh.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is not a proof for רב. It is talking about food that only looks fresh, which may even be eaten.

phrases.english: Rather, with fish that are red
phrases.notes: The gills are still red, so the fish look like they were just caught.

phrases.english: and fruit preserved in greens, we are dealing.
And why does it call them 'from that day'?
Because they are similar to things from that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the new reading of the ברייתא that the push-back in step 11 required.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the case differently (narrowing what the ברייתא is about).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about fish and fruit actually caught or picked on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means food that only looks fresh. It is not מוקצה, so it may even be eaten, which fits לוי.

steps.title: The gift is forbidden if that kind is still growing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if a גוי brings a gift on יום טוב and that kind of produce is still attached to the ground, it is forbidden. Even after יום טוב, you must wait as long as it would take to pick it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is this. If a גוי brought a gift to a Jew on יום טוב, and that same kind of food is still attached to the ground, it is forbidden. Even at night after יום טוב, it stays forbidden for the amount of time it would take to pick it.
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth between רב and לוי, רב פפא gives the final practical ruling. This first part covers produce whose kind is still growing in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If that kind of produce is still growing, we worry the גוי picked it today, on יום טוב, for the Jew. So the gift is forbidden on יום טוב itself. Even after יום טוב, the Jew must wait as long as picking would take, so he gets no benefit from work done for him on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Still attached to the ground or tree, not yet picked
The amount of time it would take to make (here, pick) them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the whole discussion. It shows that the waiting time continues even after יום טוב ends.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halacha is:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁהֵבִיא דּוֹרוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: A gentile who brought a gift to a Jew on Yom Tov,
if there is some of that same kind still attached to the ground,
it is forbidden.
And in the evening too, they are forbidden
for the amount of time it takes to make them.
phrases.notes: After יום טוב, wait as long as it would take to pick the food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was explained, רב פפא gives the practical הלכה for gifts from a גוי on יום טוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If that kind of produce is still attached, the gift is forbidden on יום טוב, and afterward you must wait as long as picking would take.

steps.title: The gift is permitted if nothing of that kind is still growing and it came from nearby
steps.stepSummary: If none of that kind is still attached to the ground, and the gift came from within the תחום, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if none of that kind of food is still attached to the ground, and it came from within the תחום, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the second half of his ruling: the case where nothing of that kind is still growing. He starts with a gift that came from within the תחום, and the sentence is setting up the case of a gift from farther away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing of that kind is still growing, the גוי could not have picked it today, so there is no picking worry. If it also came from within the תחום, no forbidden carrying from outside the boundary happened either. So the gift is fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary area a person may walk within on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's rule: if that kind is still growing, the gift is forbidden, with a waiting time after יום טוב. If nothing of that kind is still growing and it came from within the תחום, it is permitted.

phrases.english: And if there is none of that same kind still attached to the ground,
if it came from within the boundary, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: The boundary here is the area you may walk within on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the opposite case from step 13: nothing of that kind is still growing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Produce whose kind is no longer growing, brought from within the תחום, is permitted.
